hook.line: There's a new way to build custom apps without code, thanks to Zapier's newest tools.
hook.visual: Presenter at a desk by a window, talking to camera; orange 'Hot feature drop' tag over a white 'Build apps with no code' label, with phrase captions below.

beats.what: News-style opener with an orange 'Hot feature drop' label stacked on the promise.
Title card swaps to the two product names: 'Zapier Tables and Interfaces'.
Cut to a phone-filmed laptop showing the no-code app builder.
Template picker on screen with a zoom punch-in as he lists forms, portals, chatbots.
Punch-in on an 'add action / run a zap' panel.
Tool two: the no-code database table, framed as 'like a spreadsheet'.
Close zoom on the in-table buttons that trigger automations.
Back to face for the 'combine them' turn.
Screen: zaps + tables + interface stack explained as a full application.
Face again: asks viewers to say if they want a worked example.

why_it_works: A 'Hot feature drop' tag frames the ad as news, so it reads as an update rather than a pitch.
Each spoken feature cuts to the matching screen with a zoom punch (17.1 punches/min), so the eye is pointed at the exact button being named.
Clear two-part then combine structure (tool one, tool two, together) gives a payoff at the end for anyone who stays.
Ends with an offer to make a follow-up, turning comments into the next video's demand signal.
weaknesses: Screen is filmed off a laptop with a phone, so UI text is small and skewed.
Phrase captions are small (median height 0.033 of the frame) and sit on busy screen footage.
Low engagement for the reach (2,987 likes on 1.6M plays) suggests the brand-account delivery feels like an ad.
for_robert: Steal the label stack: a small coloured tag ('Hot feature drop') above a plain promise line in the first frame. Fred could slap the tag on like a sticker, then point at each punched-in button as it is named.
